definitions.explanation: A device that projects images or film onto a screen. Traditionally refers to a film projector, but also used for modern digital projectors.

examples.japanese: {映写機|えいしゃき}をセットする。
{古|ふる}い{映写機|えいしゃき}でフィルムを{上映|じょうえい}した。
examples.english: We screened a film using an old projector.

examples.japanese: {教室|きょうしつ}の{映写機|えいしゃき}が{故障|こしょう}して、{授業|じゅぎょう}で{映像|えいぞう}を{見|み}せられなかった。
examples.english: The classroom projector was broken, so we couldn't show the video in class.

notes:
Compound of {映写|えいしゃ} (projection) + {機|き} (machine). Traditionally referred to film projectors that used celluloid reels, but now also covers digital projectors. In modern everyday conversation, プロジェクター (the loanword) is more common for digital projectors, while {映写機|えいしゃき} retains a more classic or formal feel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {映写機|えいしゃき}を{回|まわ}す: to run the projector (film-era usage)
- {映写機|えいしゃき}の{光|ひかり}: the light of the projector
- {映写機|えいしゃき}を{操作|そうさ}する: to operate the projector

SIMILAR WORDS:
- プロジェクター: projector — the modern loanword, standard for digital devices
- {幻灯機|げんとうき}: magic lantern; slide projector — an older type of image projector
- {映写|えいしゃ}: projection — the act itself, without the machine
